preamble: Each domain question draws from the complete medical record. Points reflect diagnostic weight. Cost:  Small = existing record / standard echo or ECG  |  Medium = targeted test or genetic panel ($200-$1,500)  |  Large = advanced imaging CMR / EP study ($1,500-$5,000+)

questions.question: Is there unexplained LV wall thickening >=15 mm (or >=13 mm with positive family history or pathogenic variant) on 2D echo in the absence of another cause?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - the primary diagnostic criterion per ACC/AHA and ESC guidelines

questions.question: Is there asymmetric septal hypertrophy (ASH) with septal-to-posterior wall ratio >1.3 on echo?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - disproportionate septal thickening is the classic HCM morphology

questions.question: Is there systolic anterior motion (SAM) of the mitral valve on echo, with dynamic LVOT obstruction (gradient >=30 mmHg at rest or >=50 mmHg with provocation)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - present in ~70% of HCM patients; defines obstructive form (HOCM)

questions.question: Does CMR confirm LV hypertrophy distribution (apical, septal, concentric, or diffuse) and identify the morphologic subtype?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - CMR detects hypertrophy patterns missed by echo, especially apical HCM

questions.question: Is there late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) on CMR indicating myocardial fibrosis?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - LGE present in ~65% of HCM patients; extent >15% of LV mass is a major SCD risk factor

questions.question: Is there LV hypertrophy pattern on ECG (Sokolow-Lyon: SV1 + RV5/V6 >35 mm; or Cornell criteria)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - present in 75-95% of HCM patients; often the first abnormality detected

questions.question: Are there deep, narrow Q waves in the lateral or inferior leads (II, III, aVF, V4-V6) on ECG?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - 'septal Q waves' from abnormal septal depolarization; present in ~25-50% of HCM

questions.question: Are there T-wave inversions in lateral or precordial leads (particularly deep widespread inversions in apical HCM)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - deep precordial T-wave inversions (>10 mm in V3-V5) are highly characteristic of apical HCM

questions.question: Has genetic testing identified a pathogenic or likely pathogenic sarcomere gene variant (MYH7, MYBPC3, TNNT2, TNNI3, TPM1, MYL2, MYL3, ACTC1)?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - MYBPC3 and MYH7 account for ~70% of genotype-positive HCM; confirms diagnosis and enables cascade screening

questions.question: Is there a first-degree relative with confirmed HCM diagnosis or pathogenic sarcomere variant?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - ~50% transmission; triggers mandatory screening of all first-degree relatives

questions.question: Is there exertional dyspnea, chest pain, or pre-syncope/syncope on exertion?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - LVOT obstruction worsens with exercise; symptoms correlate with outflow gradient

questions.question: Is there a history of unexplained syncope, especially exercise-induced or in a young patient?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - exercise-induced syncope in HCM carries high SCD risk; triggers ICD evaluation

questions.question: Is there a family history of sudden cardiac death at a young age (<50 years) in a first- or second-degree relative?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - family SCD history is an independent risk factor in HCM SCD risk calculators

questions.question: Is the maximum LV wall thickness >=30 mm on echo or CMR?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - massive hypertrophy (>=30 mm) is a major SCD risk factor; strongly supports ICD implantation

questions.question: Is there documented non-sustained ventricular tachycardia (NSVT) on Holter or event monitor?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - NSVT on ambulatory monitoring is a major SCD risk factor per HCM Risk-SCD model

questions.question: Is there an abnormal blood pressure response to exercise (failure to rise >=20 mmHg or a drop) on exercise stress test?
questions.confirmingAnswer: Yes - abnormal BP response reflects inability to augment cardiac output; predicts SCD in young HCM patients

high.label: 🔴  80–100 High confidence
high.action: HCM confirmed; proceed to SCD risk stratification (HCM Risk-SCD score), genetic testing, and cascade family screening; CMR for LGE quantification

moderate.label: 🟡  50–79 Moderate confidence
moderate.action: CMR indicated to confirm hypertrophy pattern and assess for LGE fibrosis; genetic testing recommended; echo with provocation (Valsalva, exercise)

low.label: 🟢  <50 Low confidence
low.action: insufficient evidence; echo with provocation warranted; rule out phenocopies (Fabry, Friedreich's, athlete's heart); reassess with complete cardiac imaging before ruling out HCM
